subject: QuickPanda production: streaming parse-loop causing latency and 502s
messages:
From: Devon Lee <devon@quickpanda.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: QuickPanda Ops <ops@quickpanda.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [URGENT] Production: streaming responses truncated, latency spikes and 502s

Ben —

We started seeing a production regression at ~07:00 PDT this morning. Across our checkout flows we observe: p95 token latency jump from ~350ms to 4–6s, intermittent 502s on the call that streams completion chunks, and several downstream consumers reporting partial/malformed JSON payloads (missing closing braces). The QuickPanda client logs show repeated errors labeled "parse_loop" then a socket restart.

Attached are a short log snippet (quickpanda_error_sample.log) and a small packet capture (pcap_quickpanda_2026-07-31.zip). We haven't changed our client library in the last 48 hours. Can Redwood triage? This is impacting a subset of our traffic (~18% of requests) and causing checkout failures.

We are available for an immediate call.

—Devon

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: [URGENT] Production: streaming responses truncated, latency spikes and 502s

Triage notes (initial):
- I replayed the attached pcap and crash logs. The pattern looks like a parser state-machine re-entering header-parse on receipt of unexpected zero-length header segments (extra CRLFs from our upstream NLB keepalives).
- When the client SDK's streaming parser encounters the additional CRLF sequence mid-stream it treats it as the start of a new header block, which causes the internal framing offsets to reset. That in turn can produce partially-decoded frames and an off-by-one in the token boundary calculation. The downstream result: malformed JSON (truncated frame), parse exception, and client reconnects. Reconnects then create spike in p99/p95 latency and increase 502s under load.
- This is not a client code change on QuickPanda's side; it's an interaction between our streaming header parsing heuristic and certain intermediate keepalive behavior.

Immediate mitigation options:
1) Fast-fix in the SDK (parser) to treat isolated CRLFs inside an active body as keepalive and ignore them — low-risk patch we can hotfix in the next deploy cycle.
2) Short-term routing config: force non-chunked framed responses for QuickPanda (set header X-Redwood-Frame: true) to avoid ambiguous delimiters. This requires a routing rule and config change but no code change.
3) Telemetry: enable extended per-connection framing traces for QuickPanda to verify the fix when applied.

I'll open a JIRA and draft a hotfix PR. If we go the routing-rule route we can apply it in the next 15–30 minutes; the patch will take ~4–8 hours to get into canary and validated.

-Jonas
Senior SW Eng, Runtime

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Devon Lee <devon@quickpanda.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01T11:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QuickPanda production: streaming parse-loop causing latency and 502s

Devon — thank you for the detailed artifacts, we have an active engineering owner on this. Two immediate actions we've taken:

1) Temporary routing change: we will flip QuickPanda's route to framed responses (no chunked transfer) within the next 20 minutes. This should eliminate the ambiguous CRLF sequences while we push a proper fix.
2) Engineering will enable verbose framing traces for ~6 hours to capture the window of reproductions.

We are planning a hotfix deploy this afternoon to the SDK/runtime parser. Timeline: roll to canary at ~20:00 PDT tonight, validate, then promote based on metrics. We'll keep you updated on progress and any customer-visible changes.

If you prefer we can schedule a short joint incident call; otherwise I'll send update emails as we move through the plan.

—Evelyn

Subject: Final: Hotfix PR + canary schedule for QuickPanda

Update: PR created (https://git.redwood.internal/runtimes/stream-parser/compare/hotfix/qp-parse-loop) and JIRA-INC-6421 opened. Summary: parser will now treat an isolated CRLF sequence inside an active body as keepalive (does not reset header/frame state). Tests added for edge cases with interleaved keepalive CRLFs and small framed payloads.

Plan:
- 20:00 PDT today: deploy hotfix to Canary pool serving QuickPanda traffic (single-AZ canary).
- 22:00 PDT: evaluate canary metrics (p95 latency, 502 rate, framing trace errors).
- If stable, 02:00 PDT roll to broader pool with monitored rollback.

Rollbacks: toggle routing rule back to chunked in case of regressions; runbook attached in the PR. I'll own the rollout and will post metrics to the incident channel.

-Jonas
Senior SW Eng, Runtime
